Ava —

Appreciate the file. We can do what you asked; below is a short summary and we'll follow up with an explicit spreadsheet showing the month-by-month billing under both 50k and a temporary 20k floor.

High level:
- Billing units are counted per-token with a minimum floor applied per-account per-month (not per-request).
- We round up billing units to the nearest 100-token quantum for hosted streaming calls; non-streaming discrete calls are rounded to the nearest 10 tokens (this is consistent with our current metering).
- Prefix/KV cache reuse reduces billable tokens (we model expected KV reuse in your forecast). For bursty, short sessions the effective cost can be higher if cache hit rates are low.

Action items for us:
1) Karthik will produce the worked example spreadsheet (two scenarios: 50k min, 20k pilot min) by Thu EOD.
2) Ben will flag any concession language we need for the contract (term length, automatic reversion to standard minimums).
3) I'll propose a one-time credit mechanism to soften the first invoice if realized usage falls below the temporary minimum.

Would you prefer that the pilot exception be timeboxed (e.g., Oct–Nov) or tied to a usage threshold (e.g., until cumulative usage reaches 70k)? If you confirm, we can draft the exact contract language and a DocuSign-ready addendum.

Best,

Ava / Laura —

Attached is the worked example (sheet: "BrightCart pilot calc"). Key assumptions called out in the sheet:
- Tokenization: we used GPT-style tokenizer; sample prompts from your forecast mapped to 12–18 tokens per short call and 1.2k–3.5k tokens for long-context operations.
- Quantum rounding: hosted streaming rounds up to nearest 100 tokens; discrete API calls round to nearest 10. That means a 37-token streaming increment bills as 100; a 37-token discrete call bills as 40.
- Minimum application: monthly floor applied after aggregation across all calls; we do not apply per-route floors.
- Credit proposal: if actual billed tokens under the temporary min (20k) are lower, Redwood will apply a one-time credit on the next invoice equal to the difference between the temporary min and actual billed tokens at agreed unit rate. Credit is one-time and limited to two months.

Summary numbers (Oct forecast):
- Scenario A (standard 50k min): invoice = charge for 50k units at agreed rate = $X (see sheet).
- Scenario B (temporary 20k min with credit): invoice = charge for actual billed units unless <20k, in which case billed = 20k but a credit will be posted next invoice to net to actual usage (effectively not charging over the two-month pilot).

Ben — I left the draft concession language tab; please edit any legal/finance wording you want changed before we send this to BrightCart.
